title: Dynamic Headroom Orchestrator for Heterogeneous Memory Footprints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an orchestrator that dynamically budgets GPU memory across weights, KV cache shards, and activation buffers to maintain SLOs under mixed tenant footprints and continuous batching. The orchestrator must: (1) ingest per-tenant telemetry (sequence length distribution, batch size distribution, active KV footprint, pinned weight subsets); (2) maintain a safety corridor (headroom) computed per-GPU and per-tenant using probabilistic tail estimates; (3) provide fast reactive adjustments (within milliseconds-second) for burst events while doing gradual rebalancing for longer-term shifts; (4) expose actionable signals for preemption/eviction and tenant-level QoS tiers. Acceptance criteria: 1) no increase in 99.9th token latency > 10% across controlled A/B compared to baseline under mixed load; 2) KV eviction/unavailability events reduced by >= 35% for heavy-KV tenants; 3) memory underruns (out-of-memory) eliminated in test harness for 1000 synthetic tenant traces; 4) operator controls for target headroom percent and per-tenant min/max reservations. Constraints: cannot require model re-compilation for each tenant; must operate within existing runtime hooks (KV manager, batch router); budget calculation must be O(1) per-config step and support vectorized evaluation for fleet-wide tuning. Deliverables: design doc, simulator, integration PR(s), perf dashboard tiles, rollout playbook.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped initial design. Decided to use a two-timescale controller: probe-based micro-adjusts + nightly re-optimizer based on collected histograms.
2026-02-19 - Simulation baseline built: synthetic trace generator (sequence-length + prompt hot keys). Early sims show KV pressure spikes concentrated in 95th percentile tenants.
2026-02-26 - Design review with Runtime team: agreed to add a lightweight per-GPU sampler to avoid high-cardinality telemetry. Action: Marco to prototype sampler (ENG-468245-PR1).
2026-03-02 - Trade-off: fast preemptive eviction vs. tenant QoS. We will implement graded preemption zones (soft, hard) rather than immediate eviction to preserve tail latency for premium tenants.
2026-03-06 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248 (headroom-orchestrator core loop + sampler). Added unit tests for safety corridor math.
2026-03-10 - UX/Console sync: Console team requested a "headroom insight" tile per cluster + per-tenant advisory action (suggested reserve). Added to artifacts list.

2026-03-12 - Perf sim update: Canary simulation (1000 tenants, mixed footprints) shows 40% fewer KV evictions and 6% reduction in average token latency. Still seeing rare OOM patterns during extreme mixed bursts; next step: adaptive compaction on KV and tighter slab reclamation.
Reviewer notes (Elena Kim): please add component-level telemetry tags for correlating eviction events to kernel scheduling decisions; ensure telemetry schema change is backward compatible.
Follow-ups: tie headroom knob to cost model signals in Optimize; coordinate with Dedicated capacity planning for reserving slab spaces for enterprise tenants.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary on staging clusters (single-GPU, synthetic traffic) + smoke tests (2 days). Stage 2: gradual rollout to low-traffic host pools (10% capacity) with fast rollback flag. Stage 3: expand to mixed-tenant pools with monitoring gates (oom=0, kv-eviction<baseline). Stage 4: enable proactive rebalancing by default and expose operator knob in Console. Emergency rollback: flip runtime flag 'disable_headroom_orchestrator' and drain to baseline scheduler.
experiment_plan: A/B with control = current safety corridor; variant = orchestrator enabled. Key signals: per-tenant 99th/99.9th token latency, kv-eviction rate, per-GPU free-memory quantiles, cost delta. Run for 72h under production-matched trace replay. Use uplift alarms to automatically pause if tail latency exceeds thresholds.
next_steps: 1) Complete adaptive KV compaction prototype (Marco, 2w). 2) Add telemetry schema tags (Elena). 3) Run fleet-scale simulation (scale to 10k tenants) and produce cost-impact estimates. 4) Prepare runtime PR for review and link to console tile implementation.
